title: São Tomé and Príncipe: The Sensitive Issues Shaping 2025
excerpt: Governance, a fragile economy, oil hopes, maritime security and climate pressures: São Tomé and Príncipe faces a series of sensitive questions in 2025.
seo_title: São Tomé and Príncipe: The Sensitive Issues of 2025
seo_desc: From governance reform and oil delays to maritime security and climate threats, São Tomé and Príncipe faces a set of delicate challenges in 2025.
image_alt: São Tomé and Príncipe: the sensitive issues shaping 2025
body_html:
São Tomé, 8 December 2025—PRESS AFRICA—In 2025, São Tomé and Príncipe, a small Central African archipelago known for its relative stability, faces a series of sensitive issues that are shaping its public debate and political direction. Despite its modest size, the country is confronted with strategic challenges touching on governance, the economy, maritime security and the management of its natural resources.

Governance and institutional reform

Consolidating governance remains one of the most delicate issues. Debates over public transparency, the fight against corruption and the strengthening of institutions regularly return to the political arena. In 2025, citizens' expectations are becoming pressing in the face of slow administrative reforms and the challenge of stabilising relations between the executive and legislative branches. Civil society organisations are calling for more oversight mechanisms and citizen participation in the running of the state.

An economy under strain and structural dependence

Economically, São Tomé and Príncipe continues to depend heavily on external aid, cocoa and services. This vulnerability is a sensitive issue, especially in a context of budgetary pressure. Reforms to diversify the economy, notably towards sustainable tourism, modernised fishing and renewable energy, are moving forward but remain hampered by a lack of structural investment and limited infrastructure. Public debt and control of government spending feed political discussions.

Hydrocarbons: hopes, delays and controversy

The management of the joint oil exploration zone with Nigeria continues to raise expectations and questions. Although oil prospects have been announced for more than a decade, concrete results are slow to materialise. This uncertainty creates a climate of social frustration and fuels debate over transparency in energy agreements, foreign partnerships and financial projections. The oil question thus remains a symbol of the tension between hopes of prosperity and economic caution.

Maritime security and cross-border crime

In 2025, maritime security is among the most sensitive issues, in particular because of the country's strategic position in the Gulf of Guinea. Piracy, illegal fishing and cross-border trafficking are forcing the archipelago to strengthen its surveillance capabilities and to work more closely with regional powers. Although the situation is relatively under control, maritime vulnerability remains a national concern.

Social pressures and environmental concerns

Social issues — the cost of living, youth unemployment, the quality of public services — remain at the heart of people's demands. At the same time, environmental challenges, notably coastal erosion, deforestation and the protection of biodiversity, have become sensitive priorities in a country highly exposed to the effects of climate change. Environmental campaigners are calling for more rigorous policies to preserve the archipelago.

In 2025, São Tomé and Príncipe therefore stands at the crossroads of several crucial issues. While they represent real challenges, these matters are also opportunities to redefine the country's development and to strengthen the resilience of an island state in the midst of change.

Reporter: BAWA ALLAH Khadidjatou A.
